meta.title: Colour codes and logical teleportation

paper.authors: N. Lacroix, A. Bourassa, F. J. H. Heras et al. (Google Quantum AI)
paper.title: Scaling and logic in the color code on a superconducting quantum processor

meta.summary: Colour codes on Google's Willow processor: memories at distance 3 and 5 (error per cycle 1.71% and 1.10%, a suppression of 1.56), and logical teleportation between two colour-code patches by lattice surgery, with fidelities of 86.5–90.7%.
meta.program: The authors' own memory circuits (Zenodo, copied verbatim), and the teleportation circuit rebuilt CNOT by CNOT from the paper's Fig. 15. Every CNOT is played as H·CZ·H. After the circuit, the `decode_syndrome` system call on the decoder core; in teleportation, the frame update the paper applies in post-processing is played as a real X on the target patch, conditioned on the decoder's result.
meta.twin: The transmons each circuit uses, at the circuit's coordinates, with a coupler for every gated pair; the paper's App. B times: π/2 pulses 18 ns, π pulses 35 ns, CZ 37 ns, readout 600 ns, reset 160 ns, on RISC-Q's 2 ns grid. One RISC-Q core per transmon at 500 MHz, a frame core and the decoder core.
findings: Every operation of all three circuits ran inside its window: 3.96 µs for 3 cycles at d = 3 and at d = 5, and 7.58 µs for teleportation (805 one-qubit pulses, 362 CZs).

Under SI1000 at p = 10⁻³ (the model of the authors' noisy circuits), the error per cycle is 0.98% at d = 3 and 0.25% at d = 5 with Chromobius, against the device's 1.71% and 1.10% (neural-network decoder; 1.76% and 1.15% with its MLE decoder). The model is well below the device's noise, so the twin's suppression factor is 3.9, not 1.56.

The colour code's error model does not decompose into a matching graph, so the compiled decoder is the hypergraph union-find (cluster growth, then GF(2) elimination inside each cluster). It is far behind Chromobius: 6.0% logical error at d = 5 against 0.7%, and 11.2% against 4.3% for teleportation, on 400 noisy shots.

It is also slow: 3.69 ms in the run at d = 5 and 1.01 ms for teleportation, a median of 2.26 ms on noisy shots, against a 1.1 µs cycle. On RISC-Q's RTL in Verilator the same image takes 1.38–1.55 million cycles per decode, every host write on the same cycle as in the Lean model. Real-time decoding of colour codes needs a better decoder than this one, in firmware or in logic.
Distance 3 decomposes into a matching graph; there the compiled decoder decodes in 24.5 µs and its logical error (3.2%) is close to PyMatching's (2.9%).

One RISC-Q core per transmon keeps the 18 ns pulses on time; the cores issue ahead into their 32-entry queues. One ZCU216 holds at most 14 RISC-Q cores (riscq/board.mjs, sized from RISC-Q's RTL and Vivado records), so this twin's 18, 43 and 34 cores need at least 2, 4 and 3 boards. The Lean run keeps them on one board's hub, so syndrome bits that would cross boards arrive without the about 0.6 µs a crossing costs on RISC-Q's board-to-board network.
limits: The paper's superdense compilation merges some H layers of its CNOTs; the twin plays every CNOT as H·CZ·H, so its cycle is longer than the device's.
The teleportation run's chip placement and compilation are not given in the paper: the circuit is the one drawn in Fig. 15, placed on the 72-qubit grid by assumption.
The paper's decoders are a neural network, an MLE decoder and Chromobius; the twin's statistics use Chromobius and PyMatching, and its decoder in the run is union-find.
SI1000 is the noise of the authors' simulation, not of the device; leakage and crosstalk are not modeled.

device.title: Google Willow, the colour-code patches
device.basis: The memory circuits are the authors' own (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.14238944, copied verbatim); the teleportation circuit is rebuilt CNOT by CNOT from the paper's Fig. 15, its detectors found by Stim's flow solver. Gate, readout and reset times are the paper's App. B. A CNOT is played as H·CZ·H; the paper's superdense compilation merges some of those H layers, so the twin's cycle is longer than the paper's 1.3 µs (a stated difference). The electronics are "custom room-temperature electronics" in the paper: the controller is QuantumOS's RISC-Q model.

result0.source: "With a neural-network decoder (AlphaQubit) [24], we obtain Λ3/5=1.56(4) and ε5=0.0110(2)."

result1.source: "This is significantly lower than the logical error per cycle, ε̄3=0.0171(3), underscoring the efficiency of implementing transversal single-qubit gates."

result2.source: "Experimentally, we observe Λ3/5=1.53(4), ε̄3=0.0176(3) and ε̄5=0.0115(2), using the same MLE decoder."

result3.source: "The observed error suppression factor is in reasonable agreement with the simulated error suppression factor Λ3/5^sim=1.680(4)."

result4.source: "As expected, weight-6 stabilizers exhibit a higher error detection probability (pd,6=0.149 when averaging over all cycles and stabilizers), compared to boundary weight-4 stabilizers (pd,4=0.112)"

result5.source: "Using logical randomized benchmarking [38], we find that transversal Clifford gates add an error of only 0.0027(3), which is substantially less than the error of an idling error correction cycle."

result6.source: "obtaining an average infidelity of 0.039(3) using the Möbius decoder (Chromobius) [2] and 0.009(4) when post-selecting for runs without detectable errors (keeping on average 74.8 % of the runs)"

result7.source: "Calculating fidelity with the ideal logical states yields fidelities between 86.5(1) % and 90.7(1) % when decoded with the neural-network decoder (Fig. 5k)."

result8.source: "These measurements enable us to bound the average fidelity of the single-qubit teleportation channel, T, at F(T) ≥ 84.7(1) %"

result9.source: "We then perform the M_XX parity measurement, which involves a three-cycle lattice surgery merge operation, followed by a split operation over one cycle"

result10.source: "In the first merge cycle, two new X-basis stabilizers are added, indicated by the hatched tiles in Fig. 5d. In addition, the green (red) boundary stabilizers of L1 (L2) are expanded from weight-four to weight-six stabilizers in both bases, requiring the addition of two data qubits initially prepared in a Bell state."

result11.source: "The M_XX parity outcome is the product of the two interface X stabilizers and the additional data qubit read out in the X basis."

result12.source: "At present, the surface code achieves better logical error suppression (on the same processor, Λsc3/5=2.31(2) [3])"

result13.source: "We observe that the threshold at which the logical error per cycle for the higher distances intersect is around pth≈0.005 (see Fig. 11)."

result14.source: "Each experiment is repeated 5 000 times for 10 different initialization bitstrings: five are randomly chosen and the remaining five are their binary complements, thereby ensuring equal representation of both eigenstates for odd-distance codes."

decoding.mode: offline (inferred; not stated as a word): the neural decoder is fine-tuned on experimental data, the MLE decoder is ~1000x slower than Chromobius, and Chromobius is called only a candidate for future real-time decoding; frame updates for teleportation are applied in post-processing
decoding.decoders_quote: In this work, we explore three decoders for the color code: a möbius decoder (Chromobius) [2], a most-likely-error (MLE) decoder, and a neural-network decoder (AlphaQubit) [24].
decoding.realtime_quote: This makes Chromobius a promising candidate for real-time decoding in the near future.
decoding.speed_quote: After training, AlphaQubit can decode at an intermediate speed which is about 3 times slower than Chromobius, but 300 times faster than the MLE decoder.
decoding.mle_quote: The most-likely error is found by mapping the decoding problem onto a mixed-integer program [28, 29, Supp. 1A] which is solved with the High Performance Optimization Software (HiGHS) package [30].
decoding.teleport_decoder_quote: For state teleportation, a single instance of AlphaQubit processes the syndrome elements from both logical qubits in each cycle, along with additional syndrome elements corresponding to the stabilizers at the interface of the logical qubits during the merge cycles.
decoding.postprocessing_quote: The parity measurement outcome m1 and L1’s Z-basis measurement outcome m2 are used in post-processing to apply a conditional Pauli frame update Z_L^m1 X_L^m2 to the state of L2
decoding.postprocessing_section: VI State teleportation using lattice surgery
